# Prepare an input file with File Builder

The BCG models are calibrated for specific collection and processing protocols. Make sure you are using the BCG model that is appropriate for your samples.

*	Bugs methods [<a href="links/GP_Bug_Methods_20240730.pdf" target="_blank">PDF</a>]

*	Fish methods [<a href="links/GP_Fish_Methods_20240730.pdf" target="_blank">PDF</a>]

The File Builder joins the taxon name in the input file with the ‘original taxaID’ column in the Taxa Translator table
[<a href="https://github.com/leppott/BioMonTools_SupportFiles/tree/main/data/taxa_official/GP" target="_blank">URL</a>]
and performs two functions:

*	Translates the original taxon name to the proper OTU for the calculation.

*	Adds in new columns with taxa attributes and hierarchy (e.g., Order, Family) that are needed for the metric calculations.

Index Name and Index Class 
[<a href="links/GP_IndexNameIndexClass_20261105.xlsx" target="_blank">XLSX</a>]
are required for all calculations (they tell R which BCG rules and IBI metrics 
to apply). See tables at bottom of page.

STEP 1: CREATE THE INPUT FILE

The input file must be a comma-separated file (CSV). It can include data for
multiple samples, sites and Index Classes.

Required fields for all calculations. Column names are flexible (use drop-down menus to match).
Column Name 	Name	Data Type	Domain (allowable entries)	Description
Index_Name	flexible	text	GP_Fish_BCG, IA_Bugs_BCG, KS_Bugs_BCG, MO_Bugs_BCG, NE_Bugs_BCG	Tells R which calculation to run
Index_Class	flexible	text	see table below for list of options	Tells R which rules and metrics to apply, based on class
SampleID	flexible	text	NA (flexible)	Unique sample identifier (typically comprised of the site name, sample date, and replicate number)
TaxaID	flexible	text	NA (flexible)	Taxon name, using the BCG Operational Taxonomic Unit (OTU)
N_Taxa	flexible	numeric	non-negative real numbers; for large/rare entries, -99, 0 or blank	Number of individuals

Additional required field for IOWA BUGS only.

Column Name 	Name	Data Type	Domain (allowable entries)	Description
BugGear	Must match exactly	text	Qualitative, Surber, Hess, Artificial Substrate, Low-Flow Artificial Substrate and Anchored Artifical Substrate	Tells R whether it is a Qualitative or Quantitative sample; Qualitative + Quantitative data are included in the richness metric calculations; Quantitative only are included in the percent individual calculations


Optional fields (e.g., SiteID, latitude, longitude, collection date) can be
selected as well and will be carried through into the File Builder output file. 

IMPORTANT! Do not include Life Stage or other fields that might cause a taxon to
occur in more than one row for a given sample (which could lead to
double-counting of that taxon in the richness metrics).

INDEX_CLASSES

IMPORTANT! Capitalization scheme matters to R software (e.g., it sees 
‘Small_47c’ and ‘small_47c’ as different entries). Make sure your entries match
what is in the tables below.

Fish

|Index_Name |INDEX_CLASS	|Description|
|:----------|:------------|:----------|
|GP_Fish_BCG|Small_47c|Omernik ecoregion = Iowan Surface (47c), DrainageArea < 100 km2 (38.6 mi2)|
|GP_Fish_BCG|Large_47c|Omernik ecoregion = Iowan Surface (47c), DrainageArea >= 100 km2 (38.6 mi2)|
|GP_Fish_BCG|Small_Not_47c|Omernik ecoregion NOT Iowan Surface (47c), DrainageArea < 100 km2 (38.6 mi2)|
|GP_Fish_BCG|Large_Not_47c|Omernik ecoregion NOT Iowan Surface (47c), DrainageArea >= 100 km2 (38.6 mi2)|

Bugs
[<a href="links/BUGSonly_IndexNameIndexClass_20261105.xlsx" target="_blank">XLSX</a>]

|Index_Name	|INDEX_CLASS |Description|
|:----------|:-----------|:----------|
|IA_Bugs_BCG|CIP_medlrg_soft|Omernik ecoregion = Central Irregular Plains (CIP; 40), DrainageArea >= 75km2 (30mi2), % soft sediment (reach-scale) >= 60%|
|IA_Bugs_BCG|IowaSrf_medlrg_soft|Omernik ecoregion = Iowan Surface (47c), DrainageArea >= 75km2 (30mi2), % soft sediment (reach-scale) >= 60%|
|IA_Bugs_BCG|WCBP_medlrg_soft|Omernik ecoregion = Western Corn Belt (WCBP; 47) excluding the Iowan Surface (47c), DrainageArea >= 75km2 (30mi2), % soft sediment (reach-scale) >= 60%|
|KS_Bugs_BCG|CGP_Medium|Omernik ecoregion = Central Great Plains (CGP; 27), modeled median flow 10-100 CFS (Perry et al. 2004)|
|KS_Bugs_BCG|CIP_Medium|Omernik ecoregion = Central Irregular Plains (CIP; 40), modeled median flow 10-100 CFS (Perry et al. 2004)|
|KS_Bugs_BCG|Large|modeled median flow >100 CFS (Perry et al. 2004)
|KS_Bugs_BCG|WCBP_SmallMedium|Omernik ecoregion = Western Corn Belt (WCBP; 47), modeled median flow <10-100 CFS (Perry et al. 2004)|
|MO_Bugs_BCG|DNR_GlidePool_fall|Agency = MO DNR, Sampling Regime = GlidePool (GP), Season = fall (approx September 15-October 15)|
|MO_Bugs_BCG|DNR_RifflePool_fall|Agency = MO DNR, Sampling Regime = RifflePool (RP), Season = fall (approx September 15-October 15)|
|NE_Bugs_BCG|CGP_mNRSA|Omernik ecoregion = Central Great Plains (CGP; 27), Sampling Method = modified EPA National Rivers and Streams Assessment (NRSA)|
|NE_Bugs_BCG|RifRocky_mNRSA|Sampling Method = modified EPA National Rivers and Streams Assessment (NRSA), % Cobble >= 10% and % Riffle > 5%|
|NE_Bugs_BCG|WCBP_mNRSA|Omernik ecoregion = Western Corn Belt (WCBP; 47), Sampling Method = modified EPA National Rivers and Streams Assessment (NRSA)|
|OK_Bugs_BCG|Riffle100_ChiroC_CGP|Omernik ecoregion = Central Great Plains (CGP; 27). 100-count, riffle habitat, coarse-level Chironomidae, calibrated with small to mid-order Oklahoma Conservation Commission (OCC) samples|
|OK_Bugs_BCG|Riffle100_ChiroC_CIP|Omernik ecoregion = Central Irregular Plains (CIP; 40). 100-count, riffle habitat, coarse-level Chironomidae, calibrated with small to mid-order Oklahoma Conservation Commission (OCC) samples[JS5.1]|

STEP 2: GO TO THE ‘IMPORT FILE’ TAB AND UPLOAD THE INPUT FILE

STEP 3: GO TO THE ‘PREPARE INPUT FILE’ TAB, SELECT THE DESIRED CALCULATION, LINK
TO THE REQUIRED FIELDS IN YOUR INPUT FILE, AND RUN THE OPERATION

When the File Builder has finished running, **a prompt box** will appear. It 
will notify you if your File Builder run was successful or failed. Or, in some
cases (e.g., if there are problems with your input file), the screen will gray
out (meaning the Shiny app has crashed) and you’ll have to refresh the app,
investigate potential problems with your input file, and try again.

If your run was successful, the prompt box will alert you if there are taxa in
your input file that don’t match with the taxa list in the Taxa Translator 
table. If that happens, see instructions below for dealing with non-matching
taxa.

STEP 4: DOWNLOAD AND UNZIP THE RESULTS

A ‘results’ folder will appear, with the following subfolders:

|Folder	|Description|
|:------|:----------|
|_user_input|original input files|
|reference|taxa translator and taxa attributes, list of index names and classes|
|results_Fish_BCG	|outputs from the File Builder for fish|
|results_Bugs_IA_BCG|outputs from the File Builder for the Iowa bug BCG model|
|results_Bugs_KS_BCG|outputs from the File Builder for the Kansas bug BCG model|
|results_Bugs_MO_BCG|outputs from the File Builder for the Missouri bug BC| model|
|results_Bugs_NE_BCG|outputs from the File Builder for the Nebraska bug BCG model|
|results_Bugs_OK_BCG|outputs from the File Builder for the Oklahoma bug BCG model|

In the subfolders for each calculation, there will be four File Builder outputfiles, described below. 

|Output file	|Description|
|:------------|:----------|
|BCG_TaxaTranslator_modify|see which taxa names were modified during the Taxa Translation process (filter by Modified_woCAPS = TRUE)|
|BCG_TaxaTranslator_nonmatch|taxa in your input file that don’t match with the taxa list in the Taxa Translator table|
|BCG_TaxaTranslator_source|shows which calculation was selected, which Operational Taxonomic Unit (OTU) column was used, and which versions of the Taxa Translator and Attribute tables were used|
|BCG_TaxaTranslator_TAXAATTR|input file is now ready to go! The taxa names have been translated to the proper OTU and attributes and hierarchy added in. Import this file into the Shiny app and run the desired calculation.|


**What if there are non-matching taxa?** Open the ‘BCG_TaxaTranslator_nonmatch’
file and view the list of non-matching taxa. If the non-matches are due to a
misspelling, extra space or other small issue, fix the non-matching taxa in your
input file, re-upload the file via the ‘Import File’ tab, and rerun the File
Builder (and to prevent confusion, delete the first set of output files with the
non-matching taxa). If the non-matching taxa are legitimate taxa that need to be
added to the Taxa Translator table, notify Jen.Stamp@tetratech.com and Tetra 
Tech will update the Taxa Translator table as soon as resources permit.
